newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: China's Nat'l Petro Corp wins Caracoles oil deal.
newsitem.headline: China's Nat'l Petro Corp wins Caracoles oil deal.

text.p: China's National Petroleum Corporation bid $240.7 million Wednesday for the contract to operate Venezuela's Caracoles oil field, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said.
The bid beat a $222 million offer by Argentina's Perez Companc. A total of 14 consortia bid for the field in the third day of Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions.
The field, discovered in eastern Venezuela in 1944, currently pumps 2,700 barrels per day (bpd) from 37 active wells. Proven reserves are 218 million barrels, according to PDVSA estimates.

Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. The operator must also invest at least $12 million within three years, although PDVSA expects investment to be higher.
A total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts to be sold this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
Total bids have soared to over $1.2 billion in the three days so far, despite one auction canceled Wednesday due to lack of offers.
